context: Context and Knowledge Map, within the Practice Review
decision: Decision and Coordination Canvas, within the Practice Review
ai: AI Opportunity and Work Design Canvas, where AI proceeds to design

sense.title: Sense
sense.purpose: Notice, capture, recognise, qualify and route material signals and experience for organisational attention.
work: Notice relevant changes, weak signals, complaints and experience.
Qualify source, timing, uncertainty and possible significance.
Route the signal to people or roles able to investigate or respond.
evidence: A traceable signal, its context and a reason it matters.
A recipient, an acknowledgement and a route for exceptions.
Evidence that missing or underrepresented signals can be raised.
sense.people: Judge materiality, contribute lived experience and challenge what receives attention.
sense.ai: Detect patterns, classify incoming information and assist routing within an agreed scope.
sense.boundary: Alert volume does not establish effective sensing. Automated prioritisation needs a route for challenge.
sense.breakdown: Alerts increase, but an important problem still fails to reach anyone able to act.
sense.question: Which signals are being missed, suppressed or routed to the wrong place?

know.title: Know
know.purpose: Create, validate, locate, combine and apply relevant knowledge and expertise in context.
work: Find relevant sources and people with applicable expertise.
Validate currency, provenance, scope and disagreements.
Combine explicit information with experience to support this situation.
evidence: Sources and expertise connected to the actual work.
Current versions, applicability checks and unresolved uncertainty.
A route to correct an answer or seek additional expertise.
know.people: Interpret circumstances, supply expertise and distinguish evidence from inference.
know.ai: Retrieve and synthesise sources, suggest expertise and generate hypotheses for checking.
know.boundary: A fluent answer or successful retrieval does not establish truth, applicable expertise or decision authority.
know.breakdown: A plausible answer is used without checking whether its policy or source applies to this case.
know.question: What do we need to know, and how do we know it is applicable here?

choose.title: Choose
choose.purpose: Frame a response, evaluate alternatives and make an attributable, authorised commitment under uncertainty.
work: Frame the problem, purpose, constraints and credible alternatives.
Consider trade-offs, uncertainty, dissent and who bears consequences.
Commit, delay, monitor, experiment, escalate or deliberately take no action.
evidence: An identifiable decision owner and legitimate authority.
The decision, rationale, conditions and unresolved uncertainty.
A review trigger and a route for challenge or escalation.
choose.people: Exercise decision rights, assess alternatives and own the organisational commitment.
choose.ai: Generate options, predictions, recommendations and challenges to the reasoning.
choose.boundary: Model capability confers no organisational authority by default. Any delegation needs an explicit scope.
choose.breakdown: A recommendation is treated as approval, with no accountable decision owner.
choose.question: Who may commit the organisation, to what, under which conditions?

mobilise.title: Mobilise
mobilise.purpose: Translate an authorised commitment into coordinated, governed and reliable collective action and execution.
work: Agree responsibilities, dependencies, resources and accepted handoffs.
Execute permitted actions using the current operational state.
Detect exceptions, escalate, stop, recover and verify what happened.
evidence: Accepted responsibilities and handoffs that recipients can use.
Action records, dependencies, state and reliable completion evidence.
Defined exception, override, stop and recovery arrangements.
mobilise.people: Accept responsibility, coordinate across boundaries and exercise action and recovery authority.
mobilise.ai: Support planning and dependency monitoring; perform tool actions inside a defined execution envelope.
mobilise.boundary: Specify the acting principal, tools, data, authority, limits, evidence, approval and stop conditions, and recovery.
mobilise.breakdown: Work is marked complete while the receiving team cannot act or an exception remains unresolved.
mobilise.question: Can the commitment be carried through reliably, including when something goes wrong?

learn.title: Learn
learn.purpose: Revise organisationally available understanding, memory, routines and future response through credible feedback, reflection and inquiry.
work: Interpret evaluated consequences and compare them with expectations.
Examine rival explanations, exceptions and decision-time context.
Make warranted lessons available for subsequent decisions and work.
evidence: A scoped lesson linked to observations and its limits.
Named stewardship, correction and supersession arrangements.
Later evidence that relevant work can access and use the learning.
learn.people: Interpret consequences, contest the account, examine alternatives and steward organisational memory.
learn.ai: Analyse records, detect recurrence, retrieve previous experience and draft lessons for review.
learn.boundary: Feedback, a retrospective document or stored conversation history does not establish organisational learning by itself.
learn.breakdown: A lesson is recorded, but the next relevant case repeats the same unsupported assumptions.
learn.question: What have we learned, why do we believe it, and where will it change future work?

adapt.title: Adapt
adapt.purpose: Develop, retire or reconfigure capability, authority, structure and resources in response to credible learning and changed conditions.
work: Translate learning into implications for capability and its dependencies.
Change, stabilise or deliberately retain arrangements as evidence warrants.
Assign ownership and examine later use, reliability and unintended effects.
evidence: An explicit capability decision and accountable owner.
Changes to work, authority, resources or routines, where warranted.
Evidence from relevant later work over a stated review horizon.
adapt.people: Own resource and capability choices, institutionalisation, retirement and continued review.
adapt.ai: Propose changes, examine scenarios and support bounded experiments.
adapt.boundary: A successful pilot or scheduled review does not demonstrate persistent capability. Consider skill loss and dependency as well as speed.
adapt.breakdown: New technology or training is introduced, but work and ownership remain unchanged.
adapt.question: What should be changed or retained, and what later evidence would show that it lasts?

context.title: Contextualise
context.purpose: Relate attended signals and information to the organisational circumstances that give them meaning.
work: Connect purpose, entities, relationships and the current state.
Check history, time, evidence, relevant expertise and uncertainty.
Respect authority, access, permissions and purpose limitations.
evidence: Relevant context with source, time, scope and permission.
Material missing or disputed context made explicit.
Reconsideration when a decision, exception or condition changes.
context.people: Explain local meaning, tacit knowledge, stakeholder experience and disputed interpretations.
context.ai: Retrieve and assemble purpose-bound context with source and provenance.
context.boundary: Contextualise connects Sense and Know and recurs across the model. It is not a seventh capability or a requirement to install a knowledge graph.
context.breakdown: An accurate fact is applied to the wrong customer, policy version, time period or authority boundary.
context.question: What would we need to know about this situation to interpret the information correctly?

orientation.title: Organisational orientation
orientation.kind: Integrated state · Sufficiently shared or aligned
orientation.purpose: An account of what is happening, why it matters, what remains uncertain and what should shape response.
work: Situation and significance: what is believed to be happening, why it matters and to whom.
Uncertainty and constraints: unknowns, disagreements, purpose, authority, resources and rights.
Response conditions: what should shape action, monitoring or further inquiry.
evidence: Relevant roles can explain the situation and their response conditions.
Material disagreement and uncertainty remain visible.
The account connects to the next decision and can be revised.
orientation.people: Bring perspectives into sufficient alignment for coordinated response while preserving legitimate disagreement.
orientation.ai: Assemble evidence, compare interpretations and identify gaps for people to resolve or retain explicitly.
orientation.boundary: A document, an AI summary or unanimous agreement alone does not establish organisational orientation.
orientation.breakdown: Teams share a summary but interpret its implications differently and make incompatible commitments.
orientation.question: Do the relevant people understand what matters, what is uncertain and what should shape the response?

feedback.title: Outcomes and feedback
feedback.purpose: Turn evidence about consequences into feedback suitable for learning: output → consequence → observation → evaluation → feedback.
work: Observe intended, adverse, delayed and redistributed consequences.
Compare with a baseline or credible alternative and check implementation.
Evaluate competing explanations and state the warranted conclusion.
evidence: Whose outcomes, which work and what time horizon are covered.
Traceable observations, comparison logic and missing evidence.
Uncertainty, rival explanations and a proportionate follow-up decision.
feedback.people: Bring domain and evaluation expertise, represent affected groups and challenge favourable interpretations.
feedback.ai: Analyse records, detect differences across groups and suggest alternative explanations for testing.
feedback.boundary: A completed output or a favourable metric does not establish benefit or causality. Observation and evaluation are distinct.
feedback.breakdown: Faster handling is attributed to AI even though easier cases, staffing or policy changes may explain it.
feedback.question: What changed for whom, compared with what, and what else could explain the result?

memory.title: Organisational memory
memory.kind: Continuity infrastructure · Across all three transformations
memory.purpose: Supply prior signals, context, decisions, relationships, routines and lessons, and retain what current learning produces.
work: Preserve provenance, decision-time context and applicability.
Assign stewardship, permissions, correction and supersession.
Make relevant memory available when subsequent work needs it.
evidence: Records and routines with ownership, source, time and scope.
Current and superseded knowledge clearly distinguished.
Evidence of appropriate use, correction and transfer into later work.
memory.people: Steward memory, explain historical conditions and judge when an earlier lesson applies.
memory.ai: Retrieve and organise permitted material, identify recurrence and surface superseded information.
memory.boundary: A repository or an AI agent’s recall is not organisational memory by itself. Persistent recall creates no authority.
memory.breakdown: An old decision is reused without its assumptions, context or record of supersession.
memory.question: Can the organisation recover the right lesson, with its limits, when the next relevant situation arises?

governance.title: Purpose, governance and responsible exercise
governance.kind: Spanning conditions · Every capability and transition
governance.purpose: Make the purpose and exercise of organisational capacity legitimate, attributable, proportionate and open to challenge.
work: Make purpose, rights, representation and consequences explicit.
Define authority, evidence expectations and accountability through handoffs.
Provide challenge, appeal, correction, stop and recovery routes.
evidence: Who may decide, act, question and correct, with what authority.
Whose signals and expertise enter, and who bears consequences.
Evidence and review proportionate to the decision and its stakes.
governance.people: Exercise accountable authority, represent affected interests and maintain legitimate challenge.
governance.ai: Assist traceability, identify missing evidence and flag possible exceptions for accountable review.
governance.boundary: Effective coordination alone does not establish a legitimate purpose or acceptable consequences. Accountability must survive delegation.
governance.breakdown: A fast, coordinated process shifts harm to a group that cannot question the decision.
governance.question: Who can question the purpose, the decision and its consequences, and secure a correction?

people-ai.title: People and AI in organisational work
people-ai.kind: Participation across the model · AI is optional
people-ai.purpose: Design the contribution of people and AI around the actual work, expertise, authority and consequences.
work: Define the problem, eligible cases and a credible non-AI alternative.
Specify people’s roles and any AI objective, principal, data, tools and action limits.
Set review, challenge, stop, recovery and lifecycle ownership.
evidence: Which person reviews what, with which expertise and evidence.
Explicit authority, permitted actions and attributable records.
Outcome evaluation that includes review effort, failure and dependency.
people-ai.people: Provide expertise and accountable decisions, redesign the work and retain the ability to intervene effectively.
people-ai.ai: May support any capability through retrieval, analysis, recommendations or explicitly permitted actions.
people-ai.boundary: AI use is not a prerequisite for organisational intelligence. “Human oversight” needs a named role, evidence, authority and ability to alter the result.
people-ai.breakdown: A nominal reviewer approves recommendations without the time, expertise or authority to challenge them.
people-ai.question: Where does AI help this work, what remains with people, and how do we respond when it is wrong?

connections.title: Connection quality
connections.kind: Provisional diagnostic lens · No universal score
connections.purpose: Examine whether meaning, authority, state, evidence and accountability survive the transitions between capabilities.
work: Trace a real episode across signals, knowledge, commitments and action.
Inspect handoffs and the return of evaluated feedback to later work.
Compare connection problems with workload, incentives, resources and other explanations.
evidence: Source and recipient accounts of what was transferred and understood.
Usable context, accepted responsibility and traceable action.
Exceptions, lost information, rework and unresolved accountability.
connections.people: Reconcile meanings, accept handoffs and resolve mismatches in expertise, incentives or authority.
connections.ai: Help trace dependencies, compare records and flag inconsistencies for investigation.
connections.boundary: This is a research and diagnostic lens, not a validated universal score or the sole explanation for organisational performance.
connections.breakdown: Each team meets its own target, while authority or context disappears between teams.
connections.question: Where does the next person, team or system lose what it needs to respond well?
